class_id: a threshold constant is written in one unit and compared against a column stored in another, so every row lands in the same band
feature: any scoring, tiering, banding, alerting or gating rule whose literal thresholds were typed from how a human SAYS the quantity, while the column holds it in the unit the system STORES
symptom: a rule compares a stored value against literal thresholds a person wrote while thinking in display units — crore, thousands, MB, minutes, percent-as-0-to-100. The code type-checks, the arithmetic is valid, nothing throws, and no test fails if the fixtures were typed in the same wrong unit as the thresholds. But because real data is uniformly in the other unit and the gap is a fixed multiplier, EVERY row falls on the same side of every boundary. The output is a constant dressed as a calculation: a score that contributes no ranking, an alert that never fires or always fires, a tier everyone is in. It is not a wrong answer for some inputs, which is what testing usually looks for; it is the same answer for all of them, which reads as 'that component just isn't very discriminating'. The generic test is to feed the rule the LARGEST and the SMALLEST real stored values and assert the outputs DIFFER — a rule whose extremes agree is either unit-confused or dead. Fixture-level tests cannot find it, because the fixture and the threshold usually come from the same person's head on the same day.
first_seen: 2026-09-21 -- IPODhan item 11 (OD-20), two files with the identical defect. `web/lib/services/ipo-scoring-realtime.ts` scored issue size against 1000/500/100 and `web/lib/utils/rating-calculator.ts` against 1000/500/100 -- both CRORE figures -- while `ipos.issue_size` is stored in RUPEES. Measured read-only on ipodhan_staging: 314 of 366 rows hold a rupee-shaped value (>= 1e7), and the SMALLEST genuine row (PIYUSH, Rs0.70 Cr = 7,007,320 rupees) is still 7,007x the top threshold -- so the largest IPO on the site (NSE, Rs26,579.64 Cr) and the smallest scored IDENTICALLY. Both terms were constant across every IPO. The existing unit tests passed throughout because their fixtures were typed in crore (`issueSize: 2500, // Rs2500 Cr`) -- the same confusion as the code, so they agreed with it; the shared `mockIPOData` used 1500, meaning every OTHER test in that file was silently exercising the bottom band. `rating-calculator.ts` had NO test at all, which is why its half stayed 'documented, not fixed' (F-77) while the twin was tracked (F-95). Reached from a live API route (`app/api/ipos/[slug]/rating/route.ts`) and `scripts/calculate-ratings.ts`. A shared `RUPEES_PER_CRORE` constant already existed in `web/lib/utils.ts`, carrying a comment that says 'one calc treated it as crores' -- the class had been SEEN and the constant created, without the two call sites being changed. SECOND OCCURRENCE 2026-09-24 (F-156): web/lib/admin/dynamic-validation-rules.ts validates issueSize against 10 and 100000 CRORE while the column stores rupees; 336 of 337 staging rows trip the high warning. Root: the unit SSOT itself is wrong -- field-manifest.json tags the five OD-67 rupee columns crore -- so every consumer that trusts a label inherits the error.
fix_prs: convert at the READ using the already-shared constant (`value / RUPEES_PER_CRORE`) rather than restating the thresholds in rupees -- OD-20 makes crore the stored unit, so the crore-denominated comparison is the one that survives the coming migration and the rupee-denominated one would have to be undone. Failing tests first, written from REAL stored values rather than fixtures: 3 red on the scoring service (every case returned the maximum 0.75, including a Rs0.70 Cr IPO) and 5 red on the rating calculator (`calculateMarketScore` exported for the purpose, since an untested private function is what let F-77 survive). Then the pre-existing fixtures were corrected to rupees, because leaving them would have re-encoded the defect in the test suite. Both mutants killed by reverting the division (8 failed). ROUND 2 (2026-09-24, Tier A review REVISE): round 1's admin fix converted at the wrong edge and under the wrong key -- `web/lib/admin/amount-unit-edge.ts` looked up `issueSize`, but the dynamic admin page's real record and column keys are snake_case (`GET /api/admin/dynamic/ipos/[id]` snake_cases every key in route.ts; `column.name` from schema-introspector.ts is the Drizzle column's real DB name), so the conversion, the existing crore label and the crore validator never fired on the live page -- round 1's own tests passed only because they fed the fictitious `{issueSize}` shape. The supervisor's correction: since the live admin page has ALWAYS shown and saved raw rupees (staging ADMIN-sourced values are rupee-scale, e.g. 7,329,740,494.00), the conversion was deleted rather than re-keyed -- `amount-unit-edge.ts` and its test are gone, `web/app/admin/dynamic/[table]/[id]/page.tsx` no longer converts on load or save. Instead the label (`field-labels.ts`) and validator (`dynamic-validation-rules.ts`) got a new snake_case `issue_size` entry that is truthful about the real stored unit (label 'Rs (rupees)'; validator thresholds are the same Rs10 crore / Rs1 lakh crore bounds converted to rupees via `RUPEES_PER_CRORE`, never retyped). The old camelCase `issueSize` entries are kept only because an unrelated pre-existing suite (`dynamic-validation-rules.test.ts`) still exercises them in isolation -- they are documented as dead on the live page. `scripts/generate-field-manifest.mjs`'s `unitForField` also had a MINOR gap fixed in the same round: an unrecognised `current_unit` (e.g. a typo) silently fell through to the class default instead of failing loud; it now throws (`manifestUnitFromCurrentUnit`, unit-tested directly).
detection_check: TWO checks, corrected 2026-09-24 round 2: (1) `scripts/tests/manifest-unit-matches-current-unit.test.mjs` (`node --test`, wired into `.github/workflows/pr-gate.yml`'s 'Manifest unit follows stored unit' step, runs on every PR) -- for every column the amount-columns probe measured a current_unit for, asserts scraper/config/field-manifest.json's `unit` tag matches it, not the column's amount-class default; carries mutation tests proving a wrong tag is caught AND that an unrecognised current_unit throws rather than silently defaulting (round 2 MINOR fix). This is the schema-level companion the entry originally proposed: `docs/design/probes/amount-columns.mjs`'s current_unit field is read by the generator (`scripts/generate-field-manifest.mjs`'s `unitForField`/`manifestUnitFromCurrentUnit`), so a future column whose measured storage disagrees with its class is caught at the SSOT, not at each consumer. (2) `web/tests/unit/lib/admin/issue-size-live-key.test.ts` (part of `npm run test:unit`, runs on every PR; REPLACES round 1's deleted `amount-unit-edge.test.ts`, which drove the fictitious `{issueSize}` shape and never exercised the live page) -- drives `getFieldLabel('ipos', 'issue_size')` and `validateCustomField({ tableName: 'ipos', fieldName: 'issue_size', ... })`, the EXACT call shape DynamicFormGenerator uses, with real staging min/max rupee values, a real string-typed form value, and a direct demonstration that the dead camelCase `issueSize` validator gives the WRONG (silent) verdict on the same real low value -- proving the check discriminates and that round 1's fix was not load-bearing. Both checks now run in CI (grep-verified against `.github/workflows/pr-gate.yml` and `web`'s `test:unit` script), so `guarded` is a measured claim, not a hoped one. Neither check covers the scoring/rating pair from the first occurrence (already fixed and unit-tested per fix_prs); a future occurrence in a NEW consumer of an amount column is caught by check (1) if it reads field-manifest.json's unit, or needs its own instance of check (2)'s pattern otherwise.
